observations: Photo 0 shows a disassembled engine block with pulleys, belts, and some wiring hanging loose; heavy dirt/grease and rust-colored deposits are visible.
Photo 1 shows the top of the engine with a valve cover stamped 'DOHC 16-VALVE VARIABLE VALVE TIMING' and a Mazda winged-M logo.
Photo 2 shows a closer view of the same cover, the Mazda logo, and the air intake plenum, with grease, dust, and some orange corrosion on fasteners.
No VIN plate, engine code sticker, or displacement marking is legible in any photo.
Wiring harness ends are visibly cut/loose in photo 0, suggesting the engine was pulled from a donor car and may be missing ancillary parts.
No photo shows the engine running, the oil/coolant condition, or the underside (oil pan, flywheel, sensors).

claims.evidence: Mazda branding is visible in photo 1 and 2, consistent with a Mazda engine, but no model/engine-code plate is visible to confirm it is the Mazda 3 variant, and loose/cut wiring in photo 0 raises doubt about 'complete'.

risks.risk: Engine may not run or may have internal wear/damage.
risks.proof: A start-up video or compression test clip.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / for parts

risks.risk: Engine may be missing ancillary parts (intake manifold, sensors, turbo if applicable) given the loose cut wiring seen in photo 0.
risks.proof: Full 360° photo set showing all sides including underside and all harness connectors intact.

risks.risk: Exact engine code/displacement (e.g., 1.6L, 2.0L, 2.3L MZR) cannot be confirmed, which affects value.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine code stamp on the block or a VIN/engine tag.

risks.risk: Visible rust/corrosion on pulleys and fasteners may indicate prolonged outdoor storage or water exposure, risking internal corrosion.
risks.proof: Photo of the oil fill cap interior and a clean, de-greased shot of the block exterior.

proof_requests: Close-up of the engine code/VIN stamp on the block.
Start-up or run video of the engine.
Full set of photos from all four sides plus the underside, showing no missing ancillary parts.
Photo of oil dipstick/oil condition and coolant reservoir.
response.reason: The photos show a used Mazda engine assembly with visible branding but no model-code proof, cut wiring, and no run test, so it can be priced at worst case as an untested, possibly incomplete unit pending further proof.
